purpose: Persist authenticated TEST fixture evidence and recover a previously claimed HostedDispatch by its original reference. When Commerce qualifies a payment, Entitlements can grant one held Plan right.

implementation_revision.semantics: Provider-disabled payment evidence and authenticated known-reference recovery for the existing standalone Plan.

collaborating_domains.ownership: Owns the right derived from the committed Commerce payment consequence. Applies or replays one held Plan right under the current Privacy and correction rules.
Owns current TEST privacy suppression for each accepted party. Commerce rechecks both parties before payment application.

ash.caller_boundary: Private, source-qualified evidence writes. Only the dedicated AshOban interaction may authorize the read and worker action.
Private actions. A scheduled claim binds the loopback port, exact DER certificate and first due time. Only the dedicated AshOban interaction may authorize the read and worker action.
Private and directly authorized by Commerce after qualification. A hosted fixture payment carries its originating evidence and its lossless transaction identity.
Commerce writes an obligation with payment in one transaction. Entitlements grants from the committed source; Commerce acknowledges the owning result separately.

returns: Success after independent commit visibility, or a bounded rejection code.
side_effects: Stores digest and minimal normalized fields for the exact authenticated evidence.
caller_constraints: TEST-only Phoenix endpoint accepts POST from a loopback peer. A server-side TEST key must be configured.

returns: Success on a non-due attempt or classified observation, or retryable worker error.
side_effects: Commits the next due time and independently confirms the exact due time and round before a bounded loopback GET on a TLS connection authenticated to the original listener. Persists and processes the observation.
caller_constraints: TEST only. The persisted claim selects the original reference, port and certificate. Verify requires a certificate and a committed reservation outside any enclosing transaction.

returns: Success when terminal classification commits or replays, or a bounded error.
side_effects: Locks and classifies evidence. Ordinary charge success can establish one primary payment and consequence. A qualified excess observation stays scheduled while awaiting its primary. Once the primary qualifies it can establish one distinct collection and payer obligation.
caller_constraints: TEST only. The owner rechecks the exact scope, purchase binding, money, original reference and current party privacy.

request_flow.summary: Read the accepted quote and dispatch through the existing HostedCheckout entry. Its one claim establishes the original reference recovery schedule before sending Initialize.

The raw-body endpoint verifies the fixture signature and acknowledges only a durable receipt. Independently, the known-reference scheduler reads due claimed dispatches and issues a bounded loopback Verify. Pending evidence remains independently schedulable after either path commits.
Commerce locks and qualifies the evidence, commits payment with its consequence, and closes Verify. The existing delivery job calls Entitlements using that consequence.

guards: Authentic supported webhook or server-owned Verify response
side_effects: Insert a scoped immutable receipt and evidence identity.

guards: Claimed standalone Plan, original scope and reference, exact amount and currency, lossless transaction ID, current party privacy
side_effects: Commit or replay the single payment and its consequence.

guards: Structured pending evidence matches the claimed attempt, immutable Plan amount and currency, and original reference. Transport-only not-found, timeout, throttling and unavailable outcomes have no provider observation to qualify.
side_effects: Record the bounded reason. The known reference remains open.

guards: Unknown vocabulary, evidence mismatch or conflicting payment identity
side_effects: Store a bounded explanation with zero payment effects.
Bind the loopback port, exact DER certificate and first due time to the original reference.

guards: Due time matches a claimable dispatch
side_effects: Reserve the next attempt and check its visibility independently before HTTP. Backoff grows from 30 seconds to a 900-second cap. The fixture accepts one integer Retry-After value, clamps it to 60–900 seconds and only extends the current due time. Other forms use a 60-second fallback. Actual provider rate limiting is outside this fixture policy.
Clear the next due time in the same transaction as payment, consequence and receipt classification.

security_invariants.summary: Ingress, Verify transport and scheduler consumers compile into TEST only. Shared receipt and payment resources keep private actions. The non-TEST paid source also denies fixture payment provenance.

Only digest and bounded normalized payment fields persist. Raw bodies, credentials, headers, contact data and health data are neither retained in evidence nor sent through the fixture classifiers. SQL query telemetry is suppressed in evidence handling.

The fixture only uses fixed IPv4 loopback URLs with short deadlines, no redirect following and no automatic request retry. Scheduled Verify authenticates the exact listener certificate before sending an HTTP reference or fixture header. A closed or reused port leaves Verify open.

concurrency.summary: A receipt row lock serializes classification. A purchase lock serializes application with existing dispatch and payment operations. PostgreSQL uniquely indexes the payment purchase and fixture transaction across purchases.

Verify locks the original due dispatch and advances its next due time. It rejects explicit enclosing transactions. An independent read must see the reserved due time and round before HTTP, so an implicit Sandbox savepoint or rolled-back reservation cannot send. Queue uniqueness is advisory.

idempotency_retry.summary: Receipt identity combines fixed provider/integration/environment, source, requested reference when present and digest of the observed bytes. A changed observation may create a distinct receipt. Receipt replay remains independent of the purchase and transaction identities used for payment.

Expired or exhausted jobs leave stored obligations eligible for the next scheduler run. The payment transaction clears verification work only after qualification. Existing consequence replay returns the same held right.

failure_recovery.summary: A receipt write failure returns retryable HTTP 503. A lost reply after commit permits a fresh signature check and idempotent 202. Background receipt discovery needs no enqueue from that HTTP request.

Job absence, failed evidence insertion, timeout, throttling and a missing provider record leave the known dispatch recoverable. Fresh BEAMs resume through the original reference and replay the entitlement after the grant transaction.
The migration preserves unqualified historical rows. Rollback refuses to erase retained receipts or a recovery schedule, including the provenance that distinguishes fixture payments.

tests.proves: Exact authenticated receipt before acknowledgement and one source-qualified payment, consequence and right for a non-R399 Plan. Invalid and nonfinal evidence produces zero effects.
tests.limits: Synthetic fixture data and an isolated loopback listener. The test simulates arrival of future due times after asserting real persisted backoff, and explicitly invokes the production scheduler code via AshOban testing helpers.

cases: F-07 adjacent-version compatibility, receipt uniqueness and rollback refusal
F-05/F-07 legacy port retained and listener trust rollback refused with pending Verify
tests.proves: Isolated PostgreSQL schema proof for migration up/down/up, local foreign keys, deduplication and provenance preservation.
tests.limits: Does not reset shared data or run a provider stage.

tests.proves: The TEST ingress, workers and Verify builder are absent from non-TEST bytecode and the owner APIs deny fixture execution.
tests.limits: Build and bytecode assertion. No production release or provider call.

safe_extensions.summary: Future actual provider ingress and Verify require their own qualified scope and staged evidence under WELL-191. Preserve the dispatch identity, owning payment interface and durable recovery mechanism.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: Exclude actual Paystack calls, provider-stage promotion, imported Store Orders/Subscriptions or role bypasses, raw Repo business writes, receipt/enqueue as sole durability, replacement dispatches and generic synthetic settlement of hosted attempts. Store Paystack webhook and observation remain unimplemented at the inspected SHA.

proof_limitations: WELL-219 proof covers the standalone TEST payment foundation. WELL-221's separate Commerce refund obligation and qualification are described in commerce.fixture_refunds.json. Provider and release gates still apply.

The evidence records keep normalized fields and digests for the fixture lifetime. Tests that commit webhook receipts outside a purchase register the exact digest before ingress, so scoped P805 teardown can remove those receipts and their work. Raw bytestream capture or production retention policies require separate authority.

A legacy claim without an authenticated listener pin remains visible and cannot send a Verify request. Qualified signed evidence can still settle it. A failed TLS handshake can reach a reused loopback socket before HTTP begins.
